title: HL7-PET Hierarchy Conformance Vector
description: Schema for a single hierarchy-mode conformance vector, as defined by spec 002-hierarchy-semantics FR-007. Extends spec 001's conformance-vector.schema.json (path, message_ref, method, flags, expected, expected_lines, grammar_productions all carry the same meaning) with a required profile_ref and a semantic_rule field replacing grammar_productions' coverage-tracking role for hierarchy-specific rules. Consumed programmatically by spec 003 (regression-suite) when vectors are promoted into the shared fixtures/ corpus.

id.description: Stable, unique identifier for this vector within the whole suite, e.g. "hier-001". Distinct namespace from spec 001's path-* ids.

path.description: The PATH expression under test, using the '->' hierarchy operator (e.g. "OBR[1] -> OBX-5").

profile_ref.description: Relative path (from this spec's directory) to the synthetic segmentDefinition profile this vector is evaluated against. MUST be a profile committed under profiles/, never a real jurisdiction-specific profile from the external Scala repo.

message_ref.description: Relative path (from this spec's directory) to the synthetic source HL7 message file this vector is evaluated against. MUST point to a message satisfying FR-012 (no real patient data).

method.description: Which extraction method/variant this vector exercises.

expected.description: Expected result. For getValue: a two-dimensional array (outer = matching child occurrences, inner = field repetitions), per contracts/hierarchy-semantics.md Section A.2. For getFirstValue: a single string, or null if no match.

expected_lines.description: 1-based source line number for each value in `expected`, mirroring its shape, matching spec 001 FR-008's convention.

semantic_rules.description: Which rule(s) from contracts/hierarchy-semantics.md this vector exercises (drives spec SC-003 coverage tracking).

known_limitation.description: Name of the contracts/hierarchy-semantics.md Documented Limitation this vector demonstrates, if any (e.g. "A.4-cross-parent-child-indexing").
